title: Plotting Logistic Regression Log-Odds and Sigmoid Probabilities
description: Project each 2D sample onto its 1D linear score z = X_aug @ theta. Plot true labels and sigmoid probabilities p = sigmoid(z) along the curve, and print the fitted log-odds equation.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Compute the 1D linear scores `z = X_aug @ theta` and predicted probabilities `p = sigmoid(z)` for all `n` samples. Build `z_grid` with the supplied point count and `sig_grid = sigmoid(z_grid)`.
Plot the smooth curve `(z_grid, sig_grid)`, overlay the true `0/1` labels `y_bin + jitter` at each sample's `z` score, and mark each sample's predicted probability `(z, p)` with a black `'x'`.

Look at lines 9-10 and 28: every sample's predicted point `(z[i], p[i])` lies directly on the smooth curve `sig_grid = sigmoid(z_grid)`. This holds because `p = sigmoid(z)` evaluates that exact function at `z = X_aug @ theta`.

steps.question: At what linear score `z = X_aug @ theta` does `p = sigmoid(z)` cross one half? How does that relate to the printed log-odds `log(p / (1 - p))`?
steps.answer: `sigmoid(z)` equals one half when `z = 0`, which is also where the log-odds equal `log(1) = 0`.

steps.description: Print the 3-element parameter vector `theta` (`[-2.98914699, 1.48242428, 1.60524503]`) and format the log-odds equation `log( p / (1 - p) ) = -2.989 + 1.482*x1 + 1.605*x2`.
